packages.title: Developer Solutions
packages.subtitle: Open-source libraries for Flutter and Dart that we build and maintain. Every package is published on pub.dev under the bangertstudio.kz publisher.

items.depend: Neatly prepares everything an app needs at launch — server connection, settings, database — and hands it to the screens. Less chaos in the code, easier changes later.
items.herdsman: Automatically checks code before a developer adds it to the shared project. Mistakes and sloppy code are caught right away, not after release.
items.responsive_breakpoints: Helps an app look good on any screen — phone, tablet or computer: the interface rearranges itself to fit the size.
items.fform: A tool for forms — sign-up, checkout, questionnaires. It shows users where they made a mistake and keeps even forms with dozens of fields reliable.
items.fform_validator: Ready-made checks for form fields: is the e-mail, link, card or phone number entered correctly? Users see the error immediately instead of a rejection after submitting.
items.background_geo_tracker: Records the route even when the app is minimized and sends it to the server. Fits delivery, taxi, courier services and fitness trackers.
items.swagger_fixtures: Creates test data from the server's description, so the app can be tested without waiting for the backend. Mobile and server parts are built in parallel — the project moves faster.
items.dependency_graph: Draws a clear map of the parts a project is made of and how they connect. Helps you quickly understand someone else's or legacy code.
items.markup_analyzer: Checks an app's interface for typical slips — for example, texts nobody prepared for translation into other languages — and produces a report.
items.apollon: Keeps data up to date on every screen: change something in one place and it updates everywhere. Easy to learn, so a new team gets up to speed quickly.
items.pike: Builds the app's behaviour around clear events — "button pressed", "data arrived". The app behaves predictably and bugs are easier to find.
items.enum_picker: A ready-made interface element for choosing from a list — size, city, order status. No need to build such a list again in every project.
items.map_route: Shows all of an app's screens and the transitions between them as a diagram. A handy way to make sure users never get "stuck".
items.safe_route: Protects transitions between screens from errors: if a screen doesn't get the data it needs, the developer finds out immediately — not the user, as a crash.
items.graphview_plus: Shows connections between objects as a live interactive diagram — like Obsidian's note graph: nodes can be dragged, zoomed and explored.
items.metro_map: Draws the stages of a process as a metro map: parallel branches, where they meet and where it all leads. Fits roadmaps, funnels and task chains.

openSource.title: We publish open-source code
openSource.excerpt: We share the tools we use in our own projects: they're free and available to everyone on pub.dev.
body: We build and release open source — code that is open and available to everyone. These are Flutter and Dart tools we use ourselves in client projects.
Sharing matters to us, and we only publish our best: every package passes pub.dev checks and is maintained by our team.
It's a plus for clients too: proven solutions speed up development, and open code means your project isn't tied to one studio — any team can pick it up.

aiEstimate.title: Project estimates with AI
aiEstimate.excerpt: Our site now has a calculator: describe your idea and get a ballpark budget with every feature estimated separately.
body: We've added AI to our website to help you estimate a project before the first call. Describe your idea in your own words — the calculator breaks it into features and estimates each one.
You'll see a budget range, an approximate timeline and the team you'd need. It takes about 30 seconds, with no calls and no sign-up.
Note: this is a guideline, not a final price. Every project is unique and a precise estimate takes time — to get one, just contact us and we'll prepare a personal estimate.

faq.title: Still have

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: It depends on the scope: a landing page, a corporate site and a web service are priced differently. Get a rough range in our calculator in 30 seconds; the exact price is fixed before work starts.

items.q: How much does a mobile app cost?
items.a: The price depends on the number of screens, platforms (iOS, Android) and the backend. Describe your idea in the calculator to see the budget range, timeline and team.
The timeline depends on the task and is agreed before work starts, not after. The calculator gives a timeline estimate too.
Yes. We run research, design the interface and build a design system that your own team can take into development.

items.q: Do you work with companies from Almaty and Astana?
items.a: Yes, and with other cities of Kazakhstan too. We work remotely with regular calls, updates and project documentation.

items.q: Can BangertStudio join an existing project?
items.a: Yes. We first review the code and the current state of the product, then propose an improvement plan and join the process.

items.q: What should I prepare before we start?
items.a: A short description of the task is enough. A technical specification is optional — we'll ask the clarifying questions ourselves.
The full cycle: analytics, UX/UI design, iOS, Android, web and backend development, testing, release and post-launch support.
